findings.title: website_name bypasses untrusted-attribute hiding for TL0 profiles
findings.body: The serializer registers :website as an untrusted attribute (untrusted_attributes list, lines 105-111), so when a TL0 user's profile is restricted from anonymous viewers (scope.restrict_user_fields?), the raw :website value is omitted from the JSON. The new :website_name attribute, however, is only listed in the plain `attributes` call (line 43) and its guard `include_website_name` (line 153) only checks `website.present?`. As a result, for restricted TL0 profiles the website host plus path (e.g. 'example.com/private-page') is still serialized and rendered on the profile, leaking exactly the information the hide-profiles setting is meant to conceal. It also breaks the template: since :website is omitted, user.hbs renders `<a href="">` (empty href pointing at the current page) with the leaked website_name as the link text. website_name must be added to untrusted_attributes (or its include method must check restrict_user_fields?).

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' and is therefore dead code
findings.body: The guard is defined as `def include_website_name` but ActiveModel::Serializers only invokes include methods named `include_#{attribute}?` — every other guard in this file (include_email?, include_stats?, include_card_image_badge?, etc.) follows that convention. Because of the missing '?', this method is never called, so the intended condition (only serialize website_name when the website is present) never takes effect. When a user has no website, the JSON will still contain a `website_name: null` key, and any future restriction logic added to this guard would silently not run.

findings.title: Untrusted-attributes spec not updated for the new website_name attribute
findings.body: The test at line 11 asserts that a fixed list of untrusted attributes (bio_raw, bio_cooked, bio_excerpt, location, website, profile_background, card_background) is omitted for TL0 users viewed anonymously, but :website_name was not added to that list. Because of this gap the suite passes even though website_name leaks the website host/path for exactly the profiles the setting protects. The spec should assert `expect(json).not_to have_key(:website_name)` in that context, which would have caught the privacy regression introduced by this change.
